description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to improve learning conditions in targeted schools and strengthen the Recipient's education monitoring systems, while promoting efficiency reforms in the education sector.

The objective of the Education Reform Project for Moldova is to strengthen the quality of education while supporting the efficiency reforms being implemented in the education sector. The project has three components. (1) Strengthening the quality of education component will contribute to the strengthening of the quality of education in the general education sub sector in Moldova. (2) Improving the efficiency of the education sector component will improve the efficiency of the sector by eliminating excess capacity and creating a leaner education system, which will be better equipped to provide education that meets the demands of a modern economy. (3) Improving the Ministry of Education's (MoE) capacity to monitor the reform component will finance technical assistance (TA) for the MoE to support the implementation, monitoring and measurement of the education reform program.

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall cause MSIF to maintain, throughout Project implementation, adequate staff to support the implementation of PartA.2 of the Project, including, inter alia, a coordinator, a financial management officer, a procurement officer and anenvironmental specialist.Frequency: Continuous

The Recipient shall cause the Court of Accounts to carry out the annual financial audit of the Eligible Expenditure Program, in amanner satisfactory to the Association, and shall provide such audit financial reports to the Association, in accordance withSchedule 2 Section I.A.5 of the Legal Agreement.Frequency: Yearly

The Recipient shall ensure that MOE and MSIF carry out the Project in accordance with the provisions of the POM and shall notamend, waive or abrogate any provisions of the POM without the Association's prior approval. Frequency: Continuous

title.narrative: Schools where parents report that information, community engagement, and school responsiveness has improved

comment.narrative: The target was achieved. On May 29, 2020, the Ministry of Education and Research hired a company to conduct a survey at the national level to determine parents’ opinion if there was an improvement in information, community engagement, and school responsiveness due to use of school report cards, awareness campaigns, and other methods and tools. A total of 907 parents were interviewed by phone. The survey was conducted in 438 schools, and 311 schools (71%) reported improvement in at least one aspect. The previously reported 76.66% was reporting cumulatively for each aspect counted as share of persons, and 60% for all aspects, also considering te number of respondents.

comment.narrative: The target has been exceeded. 84% of beneficiaries (school headmasters, teachers, parents or students) who participated in planning activities during the school renovation confirm that their suggestions have been taken into account. The indicator was calculated based on the data included in the Report submitted by CIVIS Centre on the beneficiaries' survey conducted (attached). The calculation of the integrated impact indicator (the total number of the respondents in the four categories who confirm that their suggestions have been taken into account, divided by the total number of the respondents in the four categories who participated in at least one consultation event) shows that 84% of respondents who participated in planning activities during the school renovation confirm that their suggestions have been taken into account.
